headline: Recommended approval of sidewalks on Northeast Cutoff and Mountain St. East, a Mill St. discontinuance, and a Stockton St. sewer extension.
summary: The board recommended approval of sidewalk requests on Northeast Cutoff and Mountain St. East. It also recommended a Mill St. discontinuance, a guardrail at 8 Olde Millbury St., bollards at 381 Hamilton St., and a Stockton St. sewer extension. Several streetlight and other requests were recommended for leave to withdraw, held, or placed on file.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the August 25, 2026 Public Works Committee meeting, 3 yeas and 0 nays.
Recommended approval of a sidewalk on the odd side of Northeast Cutoff from 125 Northeast Cutoff to Clark St., at the applicant’s expense, 3 yeas and 0 nays.
Recommended approval, as amended, of sidewalks on the south, eastbound side of Mountain St. East from Quinapoxet Ln. to The Fairways, 3 yeas and 0 nays.
Recommended approval of the Worcester Mill LLC petition to discontinue portions of Mill St., 3 yeas and 0 nays.
Recommended approval, as amended, of a guardrail at 8 Olde Millbury St. on the Arwick Ave. side, 3 yeas and 0 nays.
Recommended approval, as amended, of two to three bollards on the Jonathan Cir. side of 381 Hamilton St., 3 yeas and 0 nays.
Recommended leave to withdraw the request to review a streetlight near 76 Copperfield Rd., 3 yeas and 0 nays.
Recommended leave to withdraw the request for additional streetlights on Lincoln St. between Norton St. and Harlow St., 3 yeas and 0 nays.
Recommended leave to withdraw the request for streetlights on Wigwam Hill Dr., which is a private way, 3 yeas and 0 nays.
Recommended leave to withdraw the request for a streetlight in front of 6 Woodcliffe Ave., 2 yeas and 1 nay (Fresolo opposed).
Recommended holding the request for an additional streetlight near 16 Kelley Sq., 3 yeas and 0 nays.
Recommended leave to withdraw the request for an additional streetlight in the vicinity of 4-18 Millbury St., 3 yeas and 0 nays.
Recommended approval of a streetlight at the intersection of Tallawanda Dr. and Brookline St., at an estimated cost of $1,500.00, 3 yeas and 0 nays.
Recommended approval of additional streetlights on North Pkwy. at Burncoat (North) Park, 3 yeas and 0 nays.
Recommended holding the request for a streetlight in front of 82 Hamilton St., 3 yeas and 0 nays.
Recommended holding the request for a streetlight in front of 73 Hamilton St., 3 yeas and 0 nays.
Recommended placing on file the petition for electronic notice of street sweeping, 3 yeas and 0 nays.
Recommended approval of “Please Pick Up After Your Dog” signage at Malden St. and West Boylston St., 3 yeas and 0 nays.
Recommended holding the petition to repair the walking path to Thorndyke Road School, 3 yeas and 0 nays.
Recommended holding the petition for No Littering signage on May St., 3 yeas and 0 nays.
Recommended holding the petition to review the sidewalk on Burncoat St., pending completion of repairs, 3 yeas and 0 nays.
Recommended placing on file the petition to change fall leaf collection and spring street sweeping, 3 yeas and 0 nays.
Recommended approval of a sanitary sewer main extension on Stockton St. at the applicant’s expense, 3 yeas and 0 nays.

CITY OF WORCESTER
Monday, September 14, 2026
PUBLIC WORKS COMMITTEE
Esther Howland (South) Chamber

Nikolin Vangjeli
COMMITTEE MEMBERS
Chairperson Tony Economou
Vice Chairperson Satya B Mitra
Councilor John P Fresolo
Joseph M. Petty
MAYOR
CLERK OF THE CITY COUNCIL
www.worcesterma.gov
City Hall - 455 Main Street  Worcester, Massachusetts
Present Were: Chairperson Councilor Tony Economou
Councilor Satya B. Mitra
Councilor John P. Fresolo
Also: Councilor Robert A. Bilotta
Commissioner of Public Works John K. Westerling
Assistant Commissioner of Engineering Jay Mello
Deputy City Clerk Stephen A.J. Pottle, clerk
. Virtual Attendee Call-In Information/Important Notice to Residents 1 
Pursuant to Chapter 20 of the Acts of 2021 and in order to ensure active, public 
engagement, the City of Worcester currently allows for both in -person and remote 
participation at all City Council and Standing Committee meetings. To partake in the 
meeting, you may attend the meeting in -person within the meeting location, follow the 
below link to join via Zoom or dial the direct line as indicated. If you join a Zoom 
meeting by dialing in with a phone number, you can raise your hand by dialing *9.
Public Works Committee Zoom Link: https://worcesterma.zoomgov.com/j/1615992759
Public Works Committee Zoom Phone Number: +1 646 828 7666
Public Works Committee Zoom Access Code: 161 599 2759
a.
Important Notice: Please be aware our office has been notified of an ongoing scam 
involving the impersonation of city officials and departments. Scammers are fraudulently 
requesting payments be made for planning and zoning permits, as well as City Council 
petitions. All official emails regarding your petition will come exclusively from an 
@worcesterma.gov email address (such as clerk @worcesterma.gov), or via physical mail 
on the City of Worcester’s official letterhead. Any legitimate hearing letter will always 
include your specific application details, along with the scheduled hearing date, time, 
and location. The City of Worcester will never request payments via wire transfer.
b.
. Approval of the Minutes 2 
Order - That the City Council Standing Committee on Public Works hereby approves the 
minutes of the Public Works Committee meeting on August 25, 2026.
a.
Chairperson Councilor Economou read the item and moved for a roll call vote to adopt the item . 
Order adopted on a roll call vote of 3 Yeas and 0 Nays
. Construct Sidewalk Petitions 3 
September 14, 2026 Page 2 of 17Public Works Committee
Councilor Tony Economou request installation of a sidewalk on the odd side of 
Northeast Cutoff from the David Clark Company at 125 Northeast Cutoff to the 
intersection of Clark St., in the interest of public safety.
# 8t CC August 18, 2026
a.
Chairperson Councilor Economou read the item and recognized the following Speakers:
1. Mark David, Project Director of David Clark Company, spoke in favor of the item
2. Fred Nathan, Worcester resident, spoke in favor of the item
Chairperson Councilor Economou recognized the Assistant Commissioner of Engineering, who 
provided an overview relative to the Department of Public Works’ (DPW) recommendation to 
approve the item at the applicant’s expense. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou discussed any further action required to approve the item, such 
as Planning Board and /or Conservation Commission approval and the feasibility of installing an 
additional Worcester Regional Transit Authority (WRTA) bus stop at the location with the 
Commissioner of Public Works, Assistant Commissioner of Engineering, and Speaker #1. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou recognized Councilor Mitra, who discussed the estimated costs 
of $125,000.00 associated with the project with Speaker #1.
Chairperson Councilor Economou discussed the existing WTRA bus stops in the general vicinity 
of the David Clark Company and the feasibility of adding infrastructure within the project to 
accommodate said bus stop with the Assistant Commissioner of Engineering. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou discussed the feasibility of expediting the approval and permit 
process for the project with Speaker #1, Assistant Commissioner of Engineering, and 
Commissioner of Public Works. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou moved for a roll call vote to accept DPW’s recommendation 
and to approve the item at the applicant’s expense. 
Recommend Approval on a roll call vote of 3 Yeas and 0 Nays
September 14, 2026 Page 3 of 17Public Works Committee
Evan Corrigan request installation of sidewalk on the eastbound side of Mountain St . 
East from the Summit to The Fairways with planting of new trees on said sidewalk.
# 7d CC March 26, 2024
b.
In Committee June 1, 2026 - Held
Chairperson Councilor Economou read the item and recognized the following Speakers:
1. Evan Corrigan, Worcester resident, spoke in favor of the item
2. Dirk England, Worcester resident, spoke in opposition to the item
3. Mike Caribo, Worcester resident, spoke in opposition to the item
4. Tim Samara, Worcester resident, spoke in opposition to the item
Chairperson Councilor Economou identified the westerly and /or southerly side of the road as the 
intended location for sidewalk installation with the Assistant Commissioner of Engineering. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou discussed the feasibility of multiple options for sidewalk 
locations, including amending the request bounds to be on the north side of Mountain St. East, 
from Briar Ln. to north of Rice St ., and ultimately, on the eastbound, south side of Mountain St . 
East, from Quinapoxet Ln. to the Fairways, with the Assistant Commissioner of Engineering.
Chairperson Councilor Economou recognized Councilor Mitra, who spoke concerning the item. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou highlighted the intent of amending the item for the purpose of 
reducing sidewalk installation bounds with the Deputy City Clerk. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou discussed the process relative for approving sidewalk 
installation requests and notifying abutters with Speaker #3 and the Deputy City Clerk. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou moved for a roll call vote to recommend the item be approved 
as amended to install sidewalks on the south, eastbound side of Mountain St. East from 
Quinapoxet Ln. to The Fairways. 
Recommend Approval as Amended to install sidewalks on the south, eastbound side of Mountain 
St. East from Quinapoxet Ln. to The Fairways on a roll call vote of 3 Yeas and 0 Nays
. Street Discontinuance Item 4 
September 14, 2026 Page 4 of 17Public Works Committee
Report of the Planning Board Upon the Petition of Mark A. Borenstein, Esq. on behalf of 
Worcester Mill LLC request discontinuance of certain portions of Mill St. as depicted on 
the attached plan and abandon the city 's right -of-way and easement rights in the 
discontinued portions of Mill St.
# 11b CC June 16, 2026
a.
Chairperson Councilor Economou read the item and recognized the following Speaker:
1. Mark A. Borenstein, Esq., Worcester resident, spoke in favor of the item
2. Fred Nathan, Worcester resident, spoke neither in favor of nor opposed to the item
Chairperson Councilor Economou recognized the Assistant Commissioner of Engineering, who 
provided an overview relative to the Department of Public Works’ (DPW) recommendation to 
approve the item.
Chairperson Councilor Economou discussed efforts made by the developer to inform abutters of 
the project and highlighted with Speaker #1. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou moved for a roll call vote to recommend the item be approved. 
Recommend Approval on a roll call vote of 3 Yeas and 0 Nays
. Guardrail Petitions 5 
Nishan Papazian request installation of bollards at 8 Olde Millbury St. on the Arwick 
Ave. side of the property in the grassy areas around the sidewalk.
# 20d CC June 2, 2026
a.
Chairperson Councilor Economou read the item and recognized the Assistant Commissioner of 
Engineering, who provided an overview relative to the Department of Public Works’ (DPW) 
recommendation to install a guardrail at the location. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou moved to amend the item to read as: “Nishan Papazian request 
installation of a guardrail at 8 Olde Millbury St. on the Arwick Ave. side of the property in the 
grassy areas around the sidewalk.”
Chairperson Councilor Economou moved for a roll call vote to recommend the item be approved 
as amended. 
Recommend Approval as Amended on a roll call vote of 3 Yeas and 0 Nays
September 14, 2026 Page 5 of 17Public Works Committee
Councilor Donna M. Colorio request installation of a guardrail on the Jonathan Cir. side 
of 381 Hamilton St.
# 8d CC October 21, 2025
b.
In Committee December 9, 2025 - Held
Chairperson Councilor Economou read the item and recognized Councilor Bilotta, who spoke in 
favor of the item. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou recognized Councilor Fresolo, who discussed the crash history 
at the location and the feasibility of installing bollards at the location in lieu of a guardrail. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou recognized the following Speaker:
1. Fred Nathan, Worcester resident, spoke in favor of the item
Chairperson Councilor Economou discussed potentially fatal impacts relative to installing 
guardrails and /or bollards to protect property in the event they are struck by a motor vehicle and 
situations where the installation of guardrails and /or bollards meets the warrants with the 
Assistant Commissioner of Engineering. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou recognized Councilor Fresolo, who discussed feasibility options 
in lieu of installing guardrails and /or bollards such as methods for reducing vehicle speed and 
increasing traffic enforcement with the Assistant Commissioner of Engineering. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou recognized Councilor Mitra, who spoke in opposition to 
granting the item Leave to Withdraw. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou moved to amend the item to read as: “Councilor Donna M . 
Colorio request installation of two (2) to three (3) bollards on the Jonathan Cir. side of 381 
Hamilton St.”
Chairperson Councilor Economou moved to recommend the item be approve as amended. 
Recommend Approval as Amended on a roll call vote of 3 Yeas and 0 Nays
. Streetlight Petitions 6 
September 14, 2026 Page 6 of 17Public Works Committee
Sherry Rice request streetlight in the vicinity of 76 Copperfield Rd. be reviewed to 
ensure it does not shine in on personal property.
# 8x CC August 18, 2026
a.
Chairperson Councilor Economou read the item and recognized the Assistant Commissioner of 
Engineering, who provided an overview relative to the Department of Public Works’ (DPW) 
recommendation to grant the item Leave to Withdraw as the department’s survey performed at 
the location did not identify intense and/or atypical residential lighting.
Chairperson Councilor Economou discussed the department’s hesitation to shut off lights in the 
interest of public safety and provided an overview relative to the light reducing measures 
previously taken at the location with the Assistant Commissioner of Engineering. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou moved for a roll call vote to accept DPW’s recommendation to 
grant the item Leave to Withdraw. 
Recommend Leave to Withdraw on a roll call vote of 3 Yeas and 0 Nays
Councilor Robert A. Bilotta request installation of additional street lighting, with a 
preference for pedestrian scale lighting, on both sides of Lincoln St. between Norton St . 
and Harlow St.
# 8h CC August 18, 2026
b.
Chairperson Councilor Economou read the item and recognized Councilor Bilotta, who

Chairperson Councilor Economou recognized the Assistant Commissioner of Engineering, who

Chairperson Councilor Economou recognized Councilor Bilotta, who discussed the addresses on 
one side of Wigwam Hill Dr. being registered as Plantation St. and the feasibility of establishing an

Chairperson Councilor Economou discussed the process relating to developing private ways in the 
city with the Assistant Commissioner of Engineering.

Councilor John P. Fresolo on behalf of Richard Molinari request installation of a

# 7b CC June 16, 2026
d.
Chairperson Councilor Economou read the item and recognized the Assistant Commissioner of 
Engineering, who provided an overview relative to the Department of Public Works’ (DPW) 
recommendation to grant the item Leave to Withdraw as there are three (3) to four (4) existing 
streetlights in both directions within one hundred fifty (150) feet and does not meet the warrants 
for additional installation.  
Chairperson Councilor Economou recognized Councilor Fresolo, who discussed the item being 
previously designated stale and highlighted resident concerns for additional lighting in the area.
Chairperson Councilor Economou recognized Councilor Mitra, who discussed DPW’s process 
relative to determine warrants for streetlight installation, an estimated cost of $2,000.00 associated 
with installing a streetlight to the existing pole in front of 6 Woodcliffe Ave ., budgetary limitations 
relating to streetlight maintenance, and the existing streetlight at 8 Woodcliffe Ave. with the 
Assistant Commissioner of Engineering and Commissioner of Public Works.
Chairperson Councilor Economou moved for a roll call vote to accept DPW’s recommendation to 
grant the item Leave to Withdraw. 
Recommend Leave to Withdraw on a roll call vote of 2 Yeas and 1 Nays (Nay – Fresolo)
September 14, 2026 Page 9 of 17Public Works Committee
Jenny Papagni request installation of an additional streetlight in the vicinity of 16 Kelley 
Sq.
# 14i CC April 28, 2026
e.
Chairperson Councilor Economou read the item and moved to take the item up collectively with 
item #6f. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou recognized the following Speaker:
1. Jenny Papagni, Worcester resident, spoke in favor of the item
2. Nick Aghapour, Worcester resident, spoke in favor of the item
3. Fred Nathan, Worcester resident, spoke neither in favor of nor opposed to the item
Chairperson Councilor Economou recognized Councilor Fresolo, who spoke concerning the item. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou discussed the two (2) damaged streetlights located in the 
vicinity of Kelley Sq. and the missing “Millbury St.” signage with Speaker #1. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou recognized the Assistant Commissioner of Engineering, who 
discussed the motor vehicle operator that struck and damaged the streetlights at Kelly Sq. being 
uninsured resulting in monetary accident recovery complications and the existing lights in the 
vicinity of the request which would not warrant for additional lighting. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou discussed safety concerns in the vicinity of 16 Kelley Sq. which 
would be alleviated by additional lighting with Speakers #1 and #2. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou discussed the process related to assessing areas for streetlight 
installation, a timeline associated with completing repairs to the two (2) damaged lights, and 
budgetary limitations relating to streetlight repairs with the Assistant Commissioner of 
Engineering. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou recognized Councilor Mitra, who discussed the estimated costs 
of $20,000.00 associated with repairing the two (2) damaged streetlights and the city’s accident 
recovery process with the Assistant Commissioner of Engineering.
Chairperson Councilor Economou brought forth the following two (2) Chairman’s Orders: “1) 
Request City Manager request Commissioner of Public Works provide City Council with a report 
detailing the city’s processes for repairing and /or replacing streetlights due to damage of any kind ; 
and 2) Request City Manager request Police Chief and the Quality of Life Team to provide 
increased attention to illegal activities occurring in the vicinity of Hotel Vernon, located at 16 
Kelley Sq.”
